Tracking RMSE increases from 0.618 to 0.950 m across reference-speed scales 0.6–1.6, illustrating the effect of reference speed on tracking accuracy under safety constraints. Additional tests examine how acceleration limits affect control effort and feasibility. These findings inform safety-filter design for UAV trajectory tracking under limited control authority.

entries.title: Federated Policy Gradient for Dynamic Consensus: Gradient Dominance and Topological Bounds
entries.abstract: This paper presents a federated optimization framework for dynamic consensus in homogeneous multi-agent systems. The underlying problem is challenged by the communication graph's spectral properties, which induce spatial heterogeneity and complicate decentralized control even when the dynamics of the agents are completely known. The problem is addressed in this paper by bridging distributed control theory with federated policy gradients. Accordingly, a comprehensive optimization landscape for dynamic consensus is established through a modal decomposition formulation. Specifically, a parameterized suboptimality bound is characterized that explicitly decouples the true aggregate policy gradient from the network covariance mismatch. Building on this formulation, sufficient conditions based on the graph's Laplacian spectrum are derived to recover exact gradient dominance, which guarantees convergence to the global consensus policy and establishes a lower bound on the achievable dominance coefficient. Furthermore, a Federated model-free consensus algorithm is proposed that utilizes zeroth-order exploration alongside a bisection-based discount factor annealing mechanism, successfully eliminating the need for an initial stabilizing policy. This approach achieves linear global convergence for policy optimization subroutines while maintaining strictly bounded outer iterations until dynamic consensus is achieved. Through extensive simulation studies and comparative feasibility analyses across diverse network topologies, it is demonstrated that the proposed federated approach consistently outperforms existing model-based and data-driven separation-based techniques.

entries.title: Gaussian Process Data-Driven Hamiltonian for Probabilistic Safe Set Construction
entries.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability is a general framework for verifying the safety of nonlinear systems, but it relies on an accurate dynamics model. The data-driven Hamiltonian (DDH) framework avoids system identification by lower-bounding the Hamiltonian directly from state-control-velocity data. However, it requires a Lipschitz bound on the unknown dynamics which is hard to certify from finite data, and as a single global constant this bound makes the computed safe sets conservative. We propose the Gaussian process data-driven Hamiltonian (GP-DDH), a fully data-driven framework that constructs safe sets with probabilistic guarantees under a GP prior on the dynamics. Furthermore, we suggest two methods to choose the confidence parameter β, both mathematically guaranteed to underbound the Hamiltonian. The computed safe set lies inside the true one with posterior probability at least 1-Δ for any Δ∈(0,1). Numerical experiments show that GP-DDH recovers a bigger volume of the true safe set than DDH while still correctly providing a conservative approximation, even when DDH is given a Lipschitz constant computed from the true dynamics.
entries.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the 9th Annual Learning for Dynamics and Control Conference (L4DC 2027)

entries.title: GreenDynaMix: Thermal-Aware Dynamic Mixed-Precision MoE LLM Inference Systems
entries.abstract: Sustained Large Language Model (LLM) inference generates significant heat that exacerbates silicon aging and reduces GPU reliability. Because GPU temperature fluctuates continuously with workload intensity and ambient conditions, keeping it in a safe range requires real-time frequency scaling, which inevitably comes at the cost of either throughput or accuracy. To address this tightly coupled challenge, we propose GreenDynaMix, the first runtime system to jointly integrate a DVFS-based thermal manager with a dynamic precision-tuning throughput compensator. A sensitivity-aware allocator leverages intrinsic importance signals from the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) router to assign higher precision to critical experts, preserving accuracy. Experiments on server, desktop, and embedded platforms demonstrate that GreenDynaMix reduces the temperature-induced aging rate of GPUs during LLM inference by 25-33%. Without offline profiling or model retraining, it recovers throughput at a perplexity cost of 0.9-1.6% with 8-bit/4-bit mixed precision, rising to 9.4% where memory forces 4-bit/2-bit.

entries.title: DAA for an Autonomous Delivery Drone: Maneuver Selection Policies for Near-Collision Risk Avoidance
entries.abstract: Detect-and-avoid (DAA) systems for autonomous drones operating in shared airspace must select avoidance maneuvers under conditions that differ markedly from those assumed by conventional DAA architectures designed for crewed aircraft. Limited on-board sensing capabilities restrict detection of collision risk to near distances (sub-km), the time available for decision-making is severely limited, uncertainty in the predicted closest point of approach (CPA) and the time to reach it is substantial, and the maneuver envelope of a small uncrewed aircraft at low altitude is tightly constrained. This paper presents and compares two maneuver-selection strategies that address these challenges: (1) a purely geometric approach, steering in the direction away from the intruder at CPA, and (2) a method that also takes into account the known sources of uncertainty in the intruder's location, and steers away from a plane expected to contain the intruder's location distribution at CPA. Performance is evaluated using the risk ratio metric on a large dataset of simulated near-collision encounters with crewed intruders. Results indicate that both strategies are feasible (i.e., computable in closed form from an onboard track estimate), and that the second strategy substantially outperforms the first.
entries.comment: 11 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication at AIAA SciTech Forum 2027, Orlando FL, Jan 11-15 2027

entries.title: Your bids are showing: re-identifying power plants in anonymized market data, and a differentially private alternative
entries.abstract: ERCOT publishes every generator's hourly offer curve 60 days after the operating day. Market monitors, researchers and traders use these records to study the merit order and check for withholding. PJM publishes the same kind of data with unit names replaced by codes, on the view that masking keeps offers confidential. We test that view on ERCOT data from 2024 to 2026, where names are public and so provide ground truth, by masking the records under PJM's published rules. Public EIA and EPA data match 25% of the masked units we can score (32% of their capacity) to their plant, and 45% fall within the top five guesses. PJM's feed carries the same fields, so we expect masking to fail there too. Publishing exact fuel-group totals instead does not help. An attacker who knows the other units in a group recovers one unit's high-price offers exactly, and an outsider who knows only the target's outage dates reaches a correlation of 0.77, most of it from a few renewable and hydro units that offer at very high prices (0.32 over fossil units). We propose a differentially private release: monthly totals by fuel group and price bin, with Gaussian noise calibrated under zero-concentrated differential privacy so that each unit's whole year of offers is protected. It publishes an unbiased noisy layer and derives a monotone supply curve and shares from it at no extra privacy cost. At ε=10 per unit-year the market supply curve stays within 11% of the truth, the implied clearing price within $3.0/MWh, and the attacker's correlation falls to 0.23. Whether an analysis still works depends on one ratio, how much the true quantity varies month to month against the noise, which predicts the accuracy of totals to within 0.05. The clearing price, supply slope and combined-cycle capacity remain usable, but no monthly release, private or exact, can answer questions about single hours or single units.
entries.comment: 14 pages, 14 figures, 2 tables

entries.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
entries.abstract: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control problem and a system identification problem. In both, exact gradients recover the optimal control and the true parameters, while the linear estimate does not, even when it accounts for spin.

entries.title: The cyborg fly: reflexes survive engineered actuators, coordination needs stand-ins
entries.abstract: Two wiring diagrams now cover the whole central nervous system of an adult fruit fly: one female, one male. Can such a diagram, run as a network of spiking neurons, drive a body? And if we swap the body's muscles for engineered actuators, what survives? We ran both connectomes, BANC and MaleCNS, as leaky integrate-and-fire networks of about 160,000 neurons each, and closed the loop through simulated sensors, actuators and bodies for walking and flight. The actuators are port-Hamiltonian, so energy is audited at every step, and swapping one for another changes only a configuration file. Null networks shuffled at five levels, from the whole nervous system to synapse counts, test whether a result depends on the wiring. The wiring produced specific functions: sugar on the labellum drove the proboscis motor neuron, leg joints resisted imposed movement, leg circuits oscillated, a looming disc drove a take-off signal on its side (in MaleCNS), and descending neurons throttled and steered flight. The resistance reflex survived 20 of 20 actuator settings in MaleCNS and 19 of 20 in BANC, including a Hill-type muscle pair and a geared DC motor; the actuator set walking speed and energy cost instead. Coordinated six-leg walking, flight stability and the correction of perturbations did not emerge. Each needed a labelled engineered stand-in, which the connectome could command. Such stand-ins can also manufacture an apparent dependence on wiring: in a rebuild of a published closed loop, odour navigation came from a hand-written rule, and the network entered only through one valence number. The two animals differed on some functions, and the differences traced to wiring, such as a haltere drive of the flight power muscles found only in MaleCNS. A whole-CNS connectome, embodied, gives reflexes, rhythms and command signals, but not the coordination that turns them into behaviour.
entries.comment: 27 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to PLOS Computational Biology. Code, configurations and figure data: Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.24302416 (public on journal publication)

entries.title: Adaptive Robust Optimisation for Frequency-Constrained Market Clearing Problem
entries.abstract: This paper formulates the day-ahead market clearing as a two-stage adaptive robust optimisation problem in which the first stage determines unit commitment, energy dispatch, and reserve procurement, while the second stage represents worst-case balancing actions under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation, load, and HVDC converter outages. Frequency security is enforced explicitly through inertia and fast frequency response constraints at the synchronous-area level, with HVDC lines allowed to provide emergency power support within their available headroom. The resulting min–max–min problem is solved by a column-and-constraint generation algorithm and applied to an eight-country North Sea test system comprising three synchronous areas, sixteen onshore bidding zones, and five offshore wind farm hubs connected through a meshed HVDC grid. We compare the Home Market (HM) and Offshore Bidding Zone (OBZ) designs on this infrastructure across different uncertainty scenarios. The results first demonstrate the value of robustness, where deterministic solutions that ignore uncertainty are severely vulnerable to worst-case realisations. Comparing the two designs, we find that OBZ's offshore zone boundaries make line congestion visible to the day-ahead market, enabling targeted reserve procurement that raises day-ahead costs but substantially reduces real-time load shedding, yielding a net reduction in total system cost that grows with the severity of localised offshore uncertainty. When both designs face the identical worst-case contingency, HM cannot distinguish an offshore converter trip from normal operation and thus fails to hedge against it, while OBZ considers the risk at the day-ahead stage. This advantage can be seasonal, scaling with the ratio of offshore wind output to HVDC line capacity and diminishing when onshore generation dominates the supply mix.
entries.comment: 33 pages, 6 figures

entries.title: Heterogeneous Risk-Sensitive Evolutionary Learning in Coordination Games: Polarization, Welfare Loss, and Intervention for Efficiency
entries.abstract: We study evolutionary learning in coordination games in a finite population of agents with heterogeneous risk attitudes, modeled using the entropic risk measure (ERM). The population consists of two subpopulations, each with a fixed risk attitude. Under risk-sensitive best response with mutations (BRM), we characterize the long-run outcomes of the learning process. In particular, we characterize when a polarized state, in which the two subpopulations choose different actions, is uniquely stochastically stable in terms of agents' risk attitudes and the subpopulation sizes. Notably, this polarized state is strictly Pareto dominated by the payoff-dominant equilibrium under both expected payoffs and agents' own ERM-adjusted payoffs. Moreover, its welfare, measured by average expected payoff, is always lower than that of the payoff-dominant equilibrium and can also be lower than that of the risk-dominant equilibrium. Thus, heterogeneity of risk attitudes in learning alone can lead to an inefficient long-run outcome. To mitigate such inefficiency, we propose intervention mechanisms to modify agents' risk attitudes in learning. We show that a sufficiently large intervention share (the fraction of agents modified) and sufficiently high intervention intensity (the increase in their risk parameter) ensure that the payoff-dominant equilibrium is uniquely stochastically stable. However, greater intervention intensity cannot compensate for an insufficient intervention share, and a larger intervention share cannot compensate for insufficient intervention intensity.

entries.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
entries.abstract: Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a Distributed Sampling-based Trajectory Optimization (DS-TO) architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to both the constraint-induced non-convexity and the decisions of other agents. The resulting algorithm is fully decentralized, requiring only neighborhood communication, with all local updates executed in parallel across agents. Efficient variations, including parallel Jacobi updates within each agent's subproblem and single-step constraint linearization, further reduce computation. Experiments on 2D and 3D tasks with up to 1024 agents demonstrate improved exploration and constraint satisfaction over state-of-the-art derivative-based distributed optimization, and superior scalability to existing distributed sampling methods.

entries.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Parameter-Varying Systems With Noisy Data
entries.abstract: This paper proposes a tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme for unknown discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems using offline noisy input-scheduling-state data. We establish a multi-trajectory simplified LPV fundamental lemma yielding a collective Hankel representation of finite-horizon trajectories. Constraining the Hankel coefficients to a scaled simplex uniformly bounds the noise-induced predictor mismatch but may exclude relevant constrained lifted trajectories. A convex-hull coverage condition for admissible receding-horizon continuations restores the required representability. LPV data-consistency and robust positively invariant sets provide tube-tightening ingredients computed directly from noisy data. The online problem is a quadratic program, for which recursive feasibility, closed-loop constraint satisfaction, and practical input-to-state stability are established. Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

entries.title: CRAB-H: Task-Centric Certification for Healthcare Autonomous Systems
entries.abstract: This paper introduces CRAB H as a task-centric certification methodology for healthcare autonomous systems. CRAB H extends the ARC governance architecture by introducing the task as a first-class governance object, represented through Task Requirement Profiles TRP H. Each profile defines the cognitive capabilities, governance constraints, evidentiary requirements, and operational assumptions necessary for the safe execution of a specific healthcare activity. Rather than asking whether a robot achieves a sufficiently high benchmark score, CRAB H asks whether demonstrated capabilities satisfy the requirements of the task. Certification becomes a comparison between demonstrated capability and required capability. A reliability-gated assurance allocation mechanism routes cognitive dimensions that cannot be reproducibly evaluated to LEA operational requirements rather than discarding them. Governance integrity is preserved: unreliable dimensions are governed, not ignored. The Capability Margin is defined as the threshold-based conjunction of per-dimension compliance determinations, not as a subtracted scalar preserving non compensatory governance logic appropriate for safety-critical healthcare deployment

entries.title: Geometric Control Analysis of an Internally Actuated Flying Wing
entries.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous geometric accessibility and controllability analysis for a fixed-wing Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) actuated solely by an internal moving mass, a momentum wheel, and external thrust. This configuration eliminates traditional control surfaces, which in turn reduces the combinatorial set of computational fluid dynamics (CFD) studies necessary for high-fidelity modeling of flight through unsteady flow fields. Using Lie bracket computations and the strong Lie Algebra Rank Condition, it is shown that the full nonlinear dynamics are generically small-time locally accessible, with singular configurations explicitly characterized and shown to be immediately escapable by direct mass actuation. The stronger property of small-time local controllability is shown to hold for the attitude subsystem at equilibrium points, using Sussmann's condition. A key contribution is the explicit treatment of the time-varying inertia tensor via the Huygens-Steiner Theorem, which introduces nontrivial coupling between the control vector fields. The momentum wheel provides direct yaw authority that, combined with inertia variation from the moving mass, generates a full-rank accessibility Lie algebra. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (MPC) is derived with consideration of flight envelope constraints and is applied to track different trajectories under unperturbed and perturbed flow field conditions.
entries.comment: Submitted to IEEE TCST for review

entries.title: Tropical Geometry-based ReLU Lyapunov Function and Controller Synthesis
entries.abstract: We investigate the joint synthesis of neural network Lyapunov functions and stabilizing controllers for systems modeled as neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODEs) with ReLU activations. Our approach leverages tools from tropical geometry, an emerging analytical framework for characterizing properties of ReLU neural networks. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to introduce tropical geometry-based methods into control theory. We represent candidate Lyapunov functions as tropical quotients of tropical signomials, which allows us to enforce the equilibrium condition at the origin and formulate constraints ensuring positive definiteness over a prescribed region of interest. We construct a total Lie surface representing the Lie derivative of the candidate Lyapunov function along the neural ODE dynamics and formulate an optimization problem to find Lyapunov parameters that ensure its negativity throughout the region of interest. This enables the systematic search for Lyapunov functions satisfying the desired stability conditions. Finally, we extend this framework to jointly synthesize a ReLU neural network stabilizing controller and a neural Lyapunov function, providing a unified approach to stability analysis and controller synthesis. We validate our proposed method on several nonlinear systems approximated as neural ODEs, demonstrating applications to Lyapunov function synthesis as well as joint Lyapunov function and controller synthesis.

entries.title: Towards a Formalised Framework for Analog Electronics and Circuit Theory
entries.abstract: Circuit theory provides the mathematical foundation for the analysis and design of electronic circuits. However, conventional circuit derivations often rely on assumptions and mathematical relationships that are not explicitly recorded, making their verification and reuse challenging. In this paper, we present the first step towards a formalised framework for circuit theory and analog electronics using the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover. As a proof of concept, we formalise an ideal RC low-pass filter, establishing reusable definitions for component impedance and circuit connections, and machine-checked theorems for voltage division, the transfer function, and low-pass behaviour. Building upon this demonstration, we outline a broader vision for an extensible library of circuit models, definitions, and verified results. Our long-term aim is to digitise, standardise, and verify circuit theory, enabling established knowledge to be systematically checked, shared, and reused across different circuit analyses.

entries.title: Topological Fairness in Continuous-State Systems
entries.abstract: Since the early days of probabilistic programs, fairness has been used to abstract randomness in software. Intuitively, a fair scheduler reproduces the almost-sure behavior of a random choice based solely on the set of possible outcomes, independent of their (often unknown) distribution. As this abstraction attaches fairness to individual transitions, it becomes ineffective over uncountable state spaces, where every single successor has probability zero. We overcome this limitation by imposing fairness on open sets instead. This leads to the novel notion of topological fairness: every basic open set—with respect to a countable basis of the state-space topology—that lies in the set of possible successors infinitely often must be visited infinitely often. We show that topological fairness carries the intuition from program abstraction to continuous state spaces. For systems with additive stochastic disturbances, almost every trajectory is topologically fair under every control policy. Reasoning over all topologically fair trajectories is therefore a sound proof principle for almost-sure properties of the original system. Unlike in the finite-state case, however, it is not complete: topological fairness cannot capture almost-sure behavior that hinges on the relative likelihoods of disturbance outcomes. Finally, we show that topological fairness supports synthesis directly on the continuous state space. For reach-avoid objectives, we give a nested fixed point over subsets of the state space which, for a broad class of systems, computes the fair winning domain exactly together with a memoryless winning strategy. Our case studies show that this winning domain is substantially larger than the one obtained with currently available techniques, which detour through a finite abstraction and certify a winning domain that depends on the discretization in a non-monotone way.

entries.title: Data-Driven Identification of Uncertainty Sets with Conformance Guarantees
entries.abstract: Formal verification and controller synthesis require accurate models. Conformance relations specify the required accuracy of a model such that properties established for the model carry over to the target system. Existing methods for establishing them from measured data are typically restricted to a single relation, a specific model class, or a downstream verification algorithm. We present ConfID, a unified framework that establishes reachset, trace, and simulation conformance with respect to measured traces by identifying uncertainty sets for a given, possibly nonlinear nominal model. Unmodeled effects are thus captured by nondeterminism rather than by refining the nominal dynamics. For all three conformance relations, the identification is a linear program that minimizes the size of the reachable sets; only its constraints depend on the relation. We further derive distribution-free bounds on the probability that the identified models are conformant for unseen behaviors. Experiments on simulated and real-world data evaluate the models identified for the three relations, confirm the guarantees, and show that these models cover unseen behaviors more reliably than baselines, with comparable or smaller sets.
entries.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE

entries.title: Marginal-Cost Clustering for Courier Dispatch: A Parallel Decomposition for Pickup and Delivery with Time Windows and Fleet Sizing
entries.abstract: Courier dispatch poses a pickup and delivery problem with time windows in which requests are batched, windows are soft, couriers start where they are and take open routes, and a fixed dispatch charge makes fleet size a decision. We contribute to the cluster-first, route-second family a grouping criterion that scores a request by its marginal cost, the travel and lateness it adds to the route a courier already plans, rather than by its distance to a centroid, one point standing for a whole workload in space and time. The marginal cost instead knows where a courier is, when it becomes free and what it already carries. Each pass, we hold the marginal costs fixed while we solve one integer program that assigns every request to a courier and chooses which to open, then improve its solution by a descent that relocates and swaps requests between couriers. We then route each dispatched courier exactly. That subproblem is naturally a mixed-integer program, and we solve it by label setting over visited sets, which we prove optimal and cheap enough to run every pass. On instances we generate and on adapted Li & Lim benchmark batches, we beat the best of six published clustering rules by 29% as published and by 12% once those rules carry the same descent. Against an adaptive large neighbourhood search at matched wall-clock we are ahead on the generated instances and level on the benchmark, and we handle 1000 requests and 300 couriers in about a minute.

entries.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Soft-Constrained AC-OPF in Multiphase Distribution Systems
entries.abstract: This paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for fast, soft-constrained AC optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems. The soft AC-OPF objective balances operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and penalties for violating operating limits. A neural network predicts distributed energy resource (DER) setpoints conditioned on operating conditions, switch configurations, and objective weights. The predicted setpoints are then processed through a DER projection and differentiable AC power flow to enforce device limits and network equalities. The framework is trained by directly minimizing the AC-OPF objective, without optimal-solution labels. Experiments on 123-, 240-, and 906-bus systems yield mean objective gaps of 0.32%, 0.92%, and 0.56%, respectively, relative to IPOPT, across wide operating ranges. Across these systems and the evaluated high-load/low-generation and low-load/high-generation scenarios, the largest mean gap is 1.04%, with mean speedups of 58-5272 times relative to IPOPT.
entries.comment: Code: https://github.com/MOSSLab-MIT/ACOPF-Multiphase-Distribution-topo-soft

entries.title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications
entries.abstract: Laypeople increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for triage advice, but LLMs answer in variable free text, which makes it hard to evaluate them for use in medical devices. Decision models, which assign a probability to each predefined triage category, may be easier to evaluate. To test their triage accuracy, we evaluated 16 decision models (14 open-weight, 2 proprietary) on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, yielding 163,728 total assessments. The best models triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real-world cases. They were more promising for recognising emergencies early: given only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, the best model reached an AUROC of 0.87. At a 5% error margin, it could decide for or against emergencies for about half of users. Decision models should therefore not replace triage engines but could shorten symptom assessments at setting-specific error margins.

entries.title: Data Center-Aware Load Pickup in Power System Restoration
entries.abstract: Data centers requiring continuous operation rely on onsite generation and battery storage during blackouts. Their return to grid supply must be coordinated with the restoration of other loads because demand fluctuations can affect system frequency. This paper adds constraints to a restoration optimization problem that coordinates load pickup, grid supply to data centers, onsite generation, and battery operation. These constraints reserve battery power and energy to accommodate bounded demand changes while maintaining approved grid supply to data centers. The method accounts for processing delays and checks resource limits using updated operating states before applying commands. Phasor-domain simulations of a low-inertia restoration scenario show that the method serves 760 MW of load outside the data centers and satisfies all tested operating limits. Nominal and frequency-aware benchmarks serve 840 MW and 800 MW, respectively, but violate operating limits.

entries.title: Constructive continuous and sampled-data control of nonstandard singularly perturbed parabolic systems
entries.abstract: The existing results on control of singularly perturbed (SP) PDE systems are all qualitative with stability guaranteed for small values of SP parameter ε, whereas control design is confined to stable fast systems. In the present paper we study the finite-dimensional output-feedback boundary stabilization of SP parabolic systems with Neumann actuators and nonlocal sensors acting on both the slow and fast dynamics. This configuration allows us to treat not only unstable fast systems, but even a larger class of nonstandard SP systems (where the fast dynamics with ε=0 cannot be solved with respect to the fast state). We design a finite-dimensional controller based on the slow descriptor PDE system. We consider the continuous-time control and, for the first time, (even for the state-feedback for SP PDEs) its sampled-data implementation. For the latter, we introduce a multi-rate sampled-data framework in which the slow and fast variables can be sampled asynchronously. We consider time-triggered control input sampling and event-triggered output sampling. We prove the avoidance of Zeno behavior and derive LMI conditions for finding upper bounds on the observer dimension, sampling control intervals and ε that preserve the stability. Our results include a new finite-dimensional controller design for the parabolic-elliptic equation. Numerical simulations demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

entries.title: Data-Driven Nonlinear Observer Design Using the Koopman Generator
entries.abstract: This paper deals with the data-driven design of nonlinear continuous-time observers using the Koopman generator. For systems without inputs, an observer is designed that consists of a linear system part with a nonlinear output injection. Therein, the output injection introduces additional degrees of freedom to ensure an invariant dictionary or a small projection error. Subsequently, this observer is extended to systems with inputs. These results form the basis for a data-driven nonlinear observer design using generator extended dynamic mode decomposition. Probabilistic finite-data error bounds are derived for the observer error w.r.t. the data-driven observer error dynamics and for the corresponding steady-state observation error. Examples of nonlinear systems with invariant and non-invariant dictionaries illustrate the effectiveness of the novel data-driven observer design procedure.
entries.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, submitted to IEEE Trans. Autom. Control

entries.title: Closed-loop Properties of Value Iteration in Continuous Time with Approximation Errors
entries.abstract: Value iteration is an important tool for approximating solutions of infinite-horizon optimal control problems, but in practice it is never carried out exactly: value functions are represented by finite-dimensional approximators, and the iteration is stopped after finitely many steps. This paper analyzes which closed-loop guarantees remain under these limitations for continuous-time nonlinear systems. We consider a value iteration scheme in which each iteration solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem with the previous iterate as terminal cost, and the associated controller applies the optimal input of this problem over each horizon in a sampled-data fashion. We show that if the convergence tolerance and the approximation error are small enough, the controller asymptotically stabilizes the system on sublevel sets of the computed iterate, and provide a suboptimality bound. This condition consists of pointwise inequalities that can be checked for the computed iterate, without establishing convergence of the iteration, and is a first step towards sample-based certification. We further establish inherent robustness of the controller with respect to model errors and recover classical results for the linear-quadratic regulator. Numerical studies on a linear-quadratic problem and on a nonlinear system with known optimal value function are consistent with the guarantees and show that the suboptimality bound is conservative.

entries.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
entries.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

entries.title: Hierarchical Multi-Timescale Deep Reinforcement Learning for QoS-Aware AI-RAN Configuration
entries.abstract: Configuring radio access networks (RANs) for heterogeneous services requires coordinating radio parameters whose effects on throughput, delay, and reliability are closely coupled and evolve over different timescales. This paper presents a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for joint, QoS-aware RAN configuration that aligns the learning structure with the real-time, near-real-time, and non-real-time control loops of O-RAN that are also adopted by AI-RAN. Three proximal policy optimization agents jointly select per-user modulation and coding schemes, user-to-bandwidth-part (BWP) assignments, per-BWP transmit power, numerology, and BWP bandwidth weights, at three timescales. The agents share a QoS-aware objective combining throughput demand satisfaction with delay and reliability penalties. We extend ns-3 5G-LENA and integrate it with Ray RLlib through ns3-ai to support the required radio controls, network observations, and hierarchical policy execution. We evaluate the agents' performance in a nine-cell downlink network with inter-cell interference, varying user populations, and mixed URLLC, gaming, conversational-video, and video-streaming traffic. Compared with the baseline 5G-NR RAN, our trained hierarchical DRL agents substantially reduce URLLC and conversational-video delays, lower the residual block error rate, and prevent the near-starvation of the weakest flows, trading off slightly lower throughput for high-rate video streaming under capacity-limited conditions.

entries.title: Power-Swing Blocking and Out-of-Step Tripping Scheme Using the Swing Center Voltage in Systems With Inverter-Based Resources
entries.abstract: Misoperation of power-swing blocking (PSB) and out-of-step tripping (OST) schemes in distance relays is a critical concern in power systems with increasing penetration levels of inverter-based resources (IBRs). Recently, several papers have studied the impact of IBRs on conventional dual-blinder PSB/OST schemes. They highlight interoperability issues concerning fast power swings and unconventional impedance trajectories, and propose revised relay settings in attempts to deal with the problems. However, the blinder-based PSB methodology suffers from being dependent on the speed of the apparent impedance just as it crosses between the blinders. It is therefore important to consider alternative methods. This paper thoroughly analyzes the characteristics of the swing center voltage (SCV) and the impacts of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) inverters on its local estimation. Then, an SCV-based PSB/OST scheme is proposed, where the main PSB criterion can be tuned from simple system parameters. This is made possible by a separate PSB activation function. The OST scheme uses only one setting and is motivated from the analytical analysis of the SCV with IBRs. Extensive PSCAD/EMTDC simulations verify the performance of the proposed SCV-based PSB/OST scheme and how it overcomes limitations of blinder-based schemes with GFM and GFL inverters.
entries.comment: 10 pages, 13 figures

entries.title: Boundary Stabilization of Mixed Traffic Flow With Connected Automated Vehicles
entries.abstract: This paper addresses boundary stabilization of stop-and-go oscillations in mixed traffic containing human-driven vehicles (HVs) and connected automated vehicles (CAVs). A penetration-dependent fundamental diagram is constructed from vehicle-class headways and effective spacing and embedded in an Aw–Rascle–Zhang (ARZ) model. Backstepping yields full-state and output-feedback controllers for the nominal linearized system. Exponential stability and finite-time convergence are established for the linearized system. Closed-loop simulations over CAV penetration rates from 0 to 1 show that increasing penetration raises the equilibrium speed and flow and reduces the convergence time for both the state-feedback and output-feedback controllers. A proportional-integral (PI) controller benchmark, input magnitude and rate constraints, physical sensor noise, and a sensitivity analysis are also considered to assess the performance of the controllers. We further illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods and the simulation framework through a fundamental diagram calibration using the TGSIM dataset. These results quantify the traffic performance changes and identify the limits of the proposed method.

entries.title: Identax: A Toolbox for Efficient Learning of Linear, Parameter-Varying, and Nonlinear Systems in JAX
entries.abstract: Accurate data-driven modelling of dynamical systems is increasingly important across engineering disciplines, yet state-of-the-art identification methods are often computationally demanding, opaque, or poorly scalable. We present Identax, a JAX toolbox for identifying linear, Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) and nonlinear systems, designed as an extensible foundation for system identification research. Its modular design allows model structures, identification criteria and optimization methods to be extended independently. The first release provides state-space and Linear Fractional Representation (LFR) models, multiple-shooting criteria for parallel training, and a transparent optimization pipeline. On the Silverbox benchmark, an LPV-LFR model outperforms all previous black-box results while training in under three minutes on a CPU. On a control moment gyroscope, Identax matches state-of-the-art accuracy.

entries.title: Passivity-Based Decentralized Stability Criterion and Active-Damping Design for DC Microgrids
entries.abstract: Interactions among converter-interfaced devices can destabilize DC microgrids (DCMGs). In practice, detailed device models often cannot be disclosed to the system operator for centralized stability analysis, and only some device controllers can be redesigned. This paper develops an output-feedback passivity (OFP)-based decentralized small-signal stability criterion for DCMGs with both fixed-controller and tunable-controller devices. By incorporating the certified OFP indices of fixed-controller devices into an equivalent network, the criterion quantifies a locally verifiable OFP requirement for each tunable-controller device. Full-order analysis further reveals that the finite current-loop bandwidth imposes upper bounds on the OFP indices of droop-controlled converters, which can remain negative for any PI gains despite positive predictions based on reduced-order analysis. Guided by the criterion and these bounds, an OFP-oriented active damping (OFP-AD) strategy is proposed for these converters. The proposed strategy improves the OFP index toward the required value while preserving the cascaded PI control and droop characteristics, using output-capacitor-current feedback. Case studies on a 39-node DCMG validate the proposed criterion and OFP-AD.

entries.title: Autonomous UAV Navigation in an Unknown Environment via Multi-Trajectory Model Predictive Control
entries.abstract: A novel model predictive control (MPC) formulation, named multi-trajectory MPC (mt-MPC), is presented and applied to the problem of autonomous navigation of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in an unknown environment. The UAV is equipped with a LiDAR sensor, providing only a partial description of the surroundings and resulting in time-varying constraints as the vehicle navigates among the obstacles. The control system layout is hierarchical: the low-level loops stabilize the vehicle's trajectories and track the set-points commanded by the high-level, mt-MPC controller. The latter is required to plan the UAV trajectory trading off safety, i.e. to avoid collisions with the uncertain obstacles, and exploitation, i.e. to reach an assigned target location. To achieve this goal, mt-MPC considers different future state trajectories in the same Finite Horizon Optimal Control Problem (FHOCP), enabling a partial decoupling between constraint satisfaction (safety) and cost function minimization (exploitation). Recursive feasibility and, consequently, persistent obstacle avoidance guarantees are derived under the assumption of a time invariant environment. The performance of the approach is studied in simulation and compared with that of a standard MPC, showing good improvement.

entries.title: IP-GNO: An Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator for Automated Distribution System State Estimation
entries.abstract: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is a crucial tool for real-time monitoring, operation, and control of the new-age distribution systems (DSs) due to intensified voltage fluctuations and operational uncertainties introduced by volatile power injection at the nodes. Existing GNN-based approaches generally exhibit limited generalization across networks with different sizes and topologies, making zero-shot cross-grid transfer to unseen DSs a significant challenge. To overcome the aforementioned challenges, this article proposes an Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator (IP-GNO) for scalable and transferable DSSE. The proposed framework frames complex bus voltage estimation as an operator-learning problem inspired by the Neumann series expansion of the inverse bus admittance matrix. An admittance-parameterized kernel, incorporating a self-admittance gate in the zeroth-order term and a persistent source-injection skip connection across network layers, captures the underlying electrical dependencies. Additionally, a Physics-Embedded Tree Encoding (PETE) scheme introduces five grid-size-invariant positional features derived from path impedance and a DC-linearized phase-angle prior. A sine-cosine output formulation is further employed to address phase-angle periodicity and ensure stable training. The proposed IP-GNO module is evaluated on two small (IEEE 33- and 69-bus), two medium (IEEE 123- and 136-bus), and one large (2522-bus) sized DSs. Particularly, its zero-shot cross-grid generalization capability is investigated by training the model exclusively on the IEEE 33-bus system and directly evaluating it on four unseen distribution networks of different sizes without retraining or fine-tuning. A detailed comparative analysis with the existing state-of-the-art DSSE tools proves the superiority of IP-GNO, enabling scalable DSSE across heterogeneous DSs.
entries.comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables

entries.title: Robust Lateral String Stability and Error Attenuation for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons
entries.abstract: Keeping an entire vehicle platoon close to its planned path is essential for navigating road boundaries and obstacles safely. Followers may rely on predecessor information for lateral guidance, which couples their lateral dynamics and allows errors to propagate downstream. This paper develops a robust lateral string stability framework to study this propagation and achieve downstream error attenuation in heterogeneous platoons under varying longitudinal motion and local perturbations. Arc-length-based feedback linearization gives each vehicle the same nominal lateral error dynamics, with parameter uncertainty and external disturbances represented as local perturbations. We define robust L₂ lateral string stability in terms of platoon-length-uniform error bounds and derive a sufficient condition for achieving it. Furthermore, we show that the same condition guarantees platoon-length-uniform L_∞ error bounds. For the considered control formulations, predecessor tracking (PT) can accumulate lateral errors, whereas desired-path tracking (DT) prevents this accumulation. We propose a learn-from-predecessor (LFP) strategy with explicit gains for downstream error attenuation and characterize how intervehicle perturbation differences limit this attenuation. Simulations validate the theoretical findings under vehicle heterogeneity, varying longitudinal motion, and local perturbations.

entries.title: Predictive Safety Filter for Multi-Modal Learned Policies
entries.abstract: This paper presents a predictive safety filter (PSF) for learned policies with multi-modal outputs. We represent the multi-modal output as a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and seek a trajectory that remains in a high-likelihood region while satisfying state and input constraints for nonlinear systems. The resulting problem is formulated as a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence minimization between the filter output and the GMM. By modeling the filter output as a Gaussian with vanishing covariance, this objective reduces in the zero-variance limit to a log-sum-exp cost, yielding a tractable nonlinear program (NLP) solved once per time step. We show that the performance degradation due to safety enforcement is bounded by a function of the worst-case KL divergence. The proposed method is validated in autonomous parking scenarios and compared with two predictive safety filter baselines: one that filters only the maximum-likelihood mode and one that filters all candidate modes and selects the best filtered one according to the finite-horizon discounted return. The proposed method achieves higher aggregate goal-reaching success than both baselines while requiring only a single NLP per step and achieving lower wall-clock time than Parallel SF in the full-mixture comparison.
entries.comment: Accepted to the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026). 6 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables

entries.title: Value function based Reward shaping for safety in quadrupeds
entries.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has progressed from simple control tasks to complex real-world challenges with large state spaces. While RL excels in these tasks, training time remains a limitation. Reward shaping is a popular solution, but existing methods often rely on value functions, which face scalability issues. This paper presents a novel safety-oriented reward-shaping framework inspired by barrier functions, offering simplicity and ease of implementation across various environments and tasks. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed reward formulations, we conduct simulation experiments on the Unitree Go1 quadruped robot in Isaacgym. The policy was better than the existing baselines and reduced safety violations from 27% to 0.1% without almost any compromise on the performance.
entries.comment: 4 pages, 6 figures

entries.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
entries.abstract: The integration of segmented energy markets into Independent System Operators (ISOs) like CAISO and MISO has increased settlement complexity. Automated transaction processing creates challenges for evaluating accuracy, compliance, and financial integrity. Traditional rule-based manual auditing is inefficient, error-prone, and cannot handle the data volume from automated markets.This research proposes Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA), a machine and reinforcement learning framework for settlement auditing via anomaly prioritization. ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions from historical market data. The approach is evaluated as an analyst-support tool for prioritizing transactions needing further audit review.ANNA was tested against traditional statistical methods, clustering-based techniques, and supervised/reinforcement learning models. The study used three years of CAISO settlement data over 63 million source records across 32 charge codes and multiple counterparties. After preprocessing, approximately 2.9 million labeled transactions formed the working dataset, with model-specific subsets used for training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using precision, recall, computational efficiency, and false-negative detection.ANNA outperforms traditional methods by identifying hidden relationships in settlement data, while standard deviation thresholds, K-Means, KNN, and Q-Learning performed poorly across key metrics. The result is a scalable solution integrating machine and reinforcement learning for automated auditing of energy market settlements, contributing computationally efficient anomaly prioritization to settlement-auditing workflows.

entries.title: Optimization of a Solar-Grid Water Supply System with Hydraulic Energy Storage: A Case Study
entries.abstract: Given the high cost of grid-scale batteries, other energy storage approaches are needed for developing and low-income regions. Elevated volumes of water are often more economically feasible energy storage options than batteries in these contexts. This paper presents a dual-framework modeling approach for one such energy storage setup: a solar-grid hybrid water supply system in the arid Afar region of Ethiopia. By utilizing an elevated 1,900 m3 water reservoir as a "hydraulic battery," the system replaces traditional electrochemical storage, significantly reducing capital expenditures. Using Python for high-resolution technical simulation and Xendee for economic optimization, the study shows a 55.1% solar fraction and a 10% Internal Rate of Return (IRR). The results confirm that hybrid systems with hydraulic storage offer a financially viable and reliable solution for water access in energy-constrained regions.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, presented at 2026 IEEE PES/IAS PowerAfrica Conference

entries.title: Voltage Ride-Through-Constrained Power Capping for Large-Scale Data Centers
entries.abstract: Large-scale data centers may satisfy steady-state network constraints while violating operational limits during voltage disturbances. This paper proposes a voltage ride-through (VRT)-aware power-capping framework that integrates AC optimal power flow scheduling with dynamic ride-through assessment. The proposed dynamic model captures converter limits, DC-link energy dynamics, battery support, and IT-bus voltage response. A simulation-based checker evaluates VRT constraints under prescribed faults, and the power caps are iteratively updated to obtain feasible schedules. Case studies on the IEEE 14-bus system with two data centers demonstrate that steady-state feasible operating points may violate transient voltage and power-import limits. Selective power capping achieves approximately 5% demand reduction during capped periods while satisfying the prescribed VRT requirements. The results highlight the necessity of incorporating dynamic security assessment into data-center operational limit determination.

entries.title: Active sensing as control over sensory acquisition
entries.abstract: The term "active sensing" is used across neuroscience and engineering to describe a wide range of sensing behaviors, but there is no consensus on what makes sensing "active." We propose that the behaviors grouped under this label are better understood as forms of control over sensory acquisition and develop a framework that distinguishes three interacting forms of control. Mechanistic control physically structures sensory input, strategic control modulates sensing in closed loop through adaptive and attentional processes, and agentic control concerns the sensing policies available to an agent and its authority to choose among them. These forms of control can occur separately or in combination, and have distinct consequences for sensory input, perception, behavior, and performance. The framework clarifies active-passive comparisons and provides a common basis for analyzing biological, engineered, and hybrid sensing systems by asking what is controlled, how, and by whom.
entries.comment: 20 pages, 4 figures

entries.title: Context-Aware Proactive Self-Adaptation: A Two-Layer Model Predictive Control Approach
entries.abstract: In self-adaptive software systems, the role of context is paramount, especially for proactive self-adaptation. Current research, however, does not fully explore context's impact, for example on priorities of the requirements. To address this gap, we introduce a novel contextual goal model to capture these factors and their influence on the system. Using this, we propose a two-layer control mechanism with a context-aware model predictive control to achieve proactive adaptation for the software system and adaptation for the controller itself. By contextual prediction and a more accurate system model, our approach utilizes model predictive control to facilitate timely and efficient system adaptations, improving both performance and adaptability. Meanwhile, we perform requirement adaptation to update the contextual goal model, which in turn updates the objective function and constraints of the controller. Our experimental evaluations across two scenarios demonstrate the significant benefits of our approach in enhancing system performance.

entries.title: Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Model Predictive and Sliding Mode Controllers on a 4-Cable Spatial CSPR in Simscape
entries.abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study between Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) applied to a spatial Cable-Suspended Parallel Robot (CSPR) actuated by four cables. The robot is modeled in two parallel ways: (i) via an analytical dynamic model with included cable elasticity and frictional losses, and (ii) in MATLAB Simscape Multibody, capturing realistic physical effects. Both controllers are implemented under identical reference trajectories, system constraints, and tuning strategies. Our results show that NMPC achieves superior tracking accuracy and stronger disturbance rejection compared to SMC, but at the cost of higher computational demand. Moreover, both controllers were tested on an analytical model of the robot and a Simscape model. The close agreement between the two, for both control schemes, confirms the accuracy of the analytical formulation and its consistency with the physics-based simulation. The study highlights the value of physics-based simulation as a complementary tool for validating advanced controllers under realistic conditions, and demonstrates that NMPC offers superior performance for the studied high-precision, constrained CSPR.
entries.comment: 7 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables. Prepared for the 13th RSI International Conference on Robotics and Mechatronics (ICRoM 2025), Tehran, Iran

entries.title: Scaled Relative Graph Separation for Unbounded Nonlinear Systems
entries.abstract: We investigate stability analysis of one-channel nonlinear feedback systems based on the recent notion of scaled relative graph (SRG). Our focus is on the SRG separation in the complex plane for feedback stability analysis that involves possibly unbounded open-loop nonlinear systems. Subject to a technical assumption, a homotopy-based SRG separation theorem is developed as the main result, where the incremental directed gap is utilized as a key instrument to quantify robust feedback stability along the homotopy path. Doing so enables us to incorporate commonly used integrators as unbounded systems in the SRG-based framework. Specializations of the main result to linear systems, along with illustrative examples, are also provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.
entries.comment: An extended version of a conference paper accepted for the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control, 2026

entries.title: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links
entries.abstract: High-dimensional quantum key distribution tolerates more noise than qubit-based protocols, but the dimension that maximizes the secret key depends on turbulence, background light, device imperfections, and block size, all of which change during an airborne or satellite pass. Finite-size security analyses of high-dimensional protocols fix the dimension in advance, and the dimension-adaptive schemes reported so far have been analyzed only asymptotically. Here, a controller sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block using only public data from earlier blocks. Each block is therefore a standard fixed-length protocol, and composable finite-key security against coherent attacks follows from sequential composition; an inaccurate channel model reduces the key rate but does not weaken security. The controller estimates turbulence from observed error rates, maximizes the expected key under forecast uncertainty, and recalibrates its model online. We evaluate it on a simulated entanglement-based orbital-angular-momentum link between an aircraft and a ground station, using Kolmogorov phase screens and the Hufnagel–Valley turbulence profile. Accounting for forecast uncertainty increases the key by 31%–47% relative to a naive planner. Over night, dawn, daytime, and model-mismatch scenarios, the recalibrated controller retains at least 98.8% of the key obtained with the best fixed dimension for each scenario, while every fixed dimension drops to 73.5% or less in at least one scenario. Running the link's measurement statistics on a superconducting quantum processor shows device errors close to a constant offset; with these errors included, the best daytime dimension changes from eight to four, and the controller adjusts accordingly.
entries.comment: 13 pages

entries.title: Feedback Completion Certificates for Repeated Dwell Tasks with Time Windows
entries.abstract: An inspection robot may owe several measurements at the same station, each with a different window in which a dwell can begin. We ask what a feedback controller must retain about earlier visits to guarantee all remaining deadlines under bounded disturbances. For a common spatial predicate and dwell length, removing redundant windows orders the remaining obligations by both endpoints. On every history without an expired obligation, the served windows form a suffix. One boundary and one capped run length therefore preserve the future satisfaction of the original task. On a verified library of branching motion primitives we use this state to recover a feedback policy. For one task type a scalar threshold per run length suffices, with work linear in the number of listed branches per time layer for fixed dwell. Multiple types require a joint recursion. On a quadrotor inspection library the threshold sweep reduced the cost of constructing a reusable full-domain policy, while a sparse Boolean baseline answered a single initial query faster. In a two-station MuJoCo patrol, three task-aware filters all met every window in twelve paired runs each. Of eight initially certified runs, the completion filter retained the certificate in all eight, compared with three for safety-only filtering.
entries.comment: 37 pages, including appendices with full proofs and experimental details

entries.title: Specification-Aware Sparse Differentiation: Planning under Signal Temporal Logic with Sparsemax Robustness
entries.abstract: Gradient-based optimal control under a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification involves solving a nonlinear program whose constraints are smoothed robustness functions of the trajectory, and automatic differentiation without knowledge of sparsity computes the Jacobian and the Hessian that its solver needs in full. This often renders the problem computationally intractable. The dynamics and the specification prescribe a sparsity pattern through the STL syntax, the windows of the temporal operators and the variables that the predicates read. Standard tools such as CasADi recover this pattern by structural detection. In this work, we propose a method to prescribe such a pattern directly from the task specification. We show that our method allows us to exploit SparseMax, a recently proposed smooth robustness operator that is certifiably sparse and sound. Its derivative is exactly zero at every operand at or below a data-dependent threshold, which structural detection cannot see. We derive the patterns that expose this trajectory-dependent sparsity to sparse automatic differentiation, with a margin test for their reuse and Hessians confined to the variables of each constraint's support. We demonstrate the method on a dual-arm coordination task in which two arms share a hand-off zone divided into cells and one until constraint per scheduled visit keeps the other arm out of a cell until the visitor has left it. The two scenes are a zone of five cells and a circle of 64 cells, with single solves and closed-loop re-planning on a rigid-body simulation. Our exact-Hessian interior-point solves are up to 27 times faster than those with the sound log-sum-exp robustness in CasADi and IPOPT.
entries.comment: 31 pages, 7 figures

entries.title: WAFT: A Fourier-Analytic Framework for Steady-State Performance of Walker Constellations
entries.abstract: The Walker configuration is predominantly adopted by nongeostationary orbit constellations exemplified by Starlink and Kuiper. The steady-state distribution of aggregate downlink interference power is critical for spectrum coexistence regulation. Large-scale time-stepped simulation and stochastic geometry (SG)-based models are the mainstream methods for obtaining the distribution, but are either computationally expensive or subject to inherent bias. This paper models the aggregate downlink interference power as an additive observable and proposes the Walker-constellation Analysis via Fourier Transform (WAFT) framework to derive the steady-state performance. Modeling the constellation as a periodic impulse array on the phase torus, the spectral representation of the observable is derived via 2-D Fourier analysis. Analytical expressions for the expectation, variance, and steady-state complementary cumulative distribution function are further derived, and the periodicity of receiver performance along longitude is characterized. For a Starlink sub-constellation example, numerical validation shows that the percentile discrepancies of WAFT relative to a finite-duration time-stepped simulation remain within 0.09 dB. Comparisons with isotropic and intensity-matched SG models reveal that the conditional independence of satellite positions alone makes the models assign a substantial probability mass to physically infeasible values, producing percentile discrepancies.

entries.title: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment
entries.abstract: In near-field physical-layer authentication (PLA), the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. With a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can cause the false rejection (FR) probability to approach one as the received energy increases. We derive the distribution of the overlap between the true and enrolled spatial directions and use it to calibrate a test based on the aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. The calibration bounds FR for arbitrary regional gains and all legitimate received energies above a prescribed minimum. For a fixed enrolled reference, we reduce the problem of finding the maximum acceptance probability of a multi-antenna attacker to a one-dimensional search. We also derive a pre-enrollment upper bound that holds when the attacker chooses its precoder after observing the enrolled reference. For a single region and a fixed angular threshold, the enrollment energy sufficient to preserve angular separation grows inversely with the square of the available angular margin. In the numerical study with 128 receive elements at 28 GHz, the FR upper bound was 0.9984, including the enrollment outage allowance. At a regional phase perturbation of 20, four regions provided the best trade-off among the tested partitions: its simulated FR was 0.1442, while its false acceptance (FA) at 9 m was 1.084 under the fixed transmit-energy setting.

entries.title: SatMend: LLM Agents for Automated Software Repair in Satellite Constellations with Intermittent Ground Contact
entries.abstract: Satellite constellations rely on onboard software to sustain services across cooperating spacecraft. Maintaining this software requires handling related component versions and different failure causes while delivering repairs through intermittent ground contact. Automated software repair in satellite constellations remains underexplored, particularly the coordination of repairs across related versions with verified onboard recovery under intermittent ground contact. To address this gap, we propose SatMend, a software repair method driven by ground-based large language model (LLM) agents. SatMend organizes related versions into persistent sessions to retain diagnostic context and combines source and runtime evidence to select code repair or state recovery actions. It validates each version separately and submits ready candidates during continued repair, allowing ground preparation to overlap with onboard delivery and verification. Experimental results show that across configurations with 16 to 64 satellites, SatMend restores 192 of 224 faulty applications within 600 s, compared with 40 for SWE-agent, 77 for Agentless, 124 for RepairAgent, and 115 for SWE-Search. These results demonstrate SatMend's effectiveness in restoring applications and supporting service continuity in satellite constellations with intermittent ground contact.

entries.title: Analysis of Geometric Eigenmode Splitting in Planar Microwave Resonators
entries.abstract: A traditional challenge in planar microwave resonator design is to find geometric mechanisms that can control individual resonant frequencies - or tune coupling between specific eigenmodes - without affecting other system parameters, such as the center frequency. Achieving this capability can be transformative for the design of microwave sensors, filters, antennas and resonant networks. Starting from first principles, we outline the development of an analytical method that guides practical design by suggesting specific perturbation shapes capable of achieving resonant mode-splitting while keeping the center frequency nearly stationary. This approach opens the door to novel designs that were previously difficult to discover or optimize. Independent numerical simulations and measurements of stripline resonators validate the effectiveness of this approach. The demonstrated tuning effect shows that the first-order estimate suggested by the theory persists in practice over a relatively wide splitting bandwidth (exceeding 54% of center frequency), increasing the utility of the proposed method.
entries.comment: 4 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables

entries.title: Implementation and Software-in-the-Loop Evaluation of a Trans-Domain Digital Twin Architecture for Autonomous Guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV Without Online GNSS
entries.abstract: Autonomous UAV guidance in emergency response, infrastructure monitoring, and cargo transportation requires reliable navigation. However, satellite-based positioning may become unavailable or unreliable in enclosed spaces, blind spots caused by natural obstacles and structures, and environments affected by radio interference and signal spoofing during electronic warfare. This study designs, implements, and evaluates a system based on a Trans-Domain Digital Twin (TDDT) for autonomous guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV. Independent navigation, flight dynamics, and meteorological models are coordinated within a cycle of state estimation, prediction, decision-making, command execution, and feedback. Data from inertial, magnetic, pressure, and airspeed sensors, together with environmental information, form the basis for estimation and prediction. Furthermore, a shared state, temporal synchronization, preservation of information provenance, and command traceability establish continuity between models and decisions. The system was tested with a simulated physical twin in a software-in-the-loop environment. Vertical takeoff, movement toward the destination, landing, and autonomous stopping were recorded, and the dynamic model was adjusted to a limited extent based on sensor-derived feedback. Separating the evaluation reference from navigation inputs enabled independent assessment of positioning error and computational performance. The results confirm operational coordination, decision traceability, and closed-loop guidance under the tested conditions, providing a reproducible platform for the development and evaluation of navigation without satellite-based positioning.
